question: Can a non-parametric empirical CDF mapping of the margin distribution predict ranking agreement at n=15 and n=20 within 10pp, providing a validated extrapolation path to full-DOM n=50/82 — or should the Intel lane pivot to prioritize Docker-based direct full-DOM measurement to bypass modeling entirely?
hypothesis: Three consecutive parametric SNR decompositions (Phi(mean/std), Phi(median/std), saturating power law) have been REJECTED at C1. The step-function structure of proportion(margin>0) — (0, 0, 0.50, 0.57) at n=5/10/15/20 — suggests a threshold/phase-transition mechanism rather than smooth parametric form. An empirical CDF mapping F_empirical: n -> proportion(margin>0) uses the observed data directly without functional form assumptions, capturing the step-function structure that parametric models miss. H1: The empirical CDF interpolation at n=15 and n=20 reproduces observed agreement within 10pp (trivially true by construction at training points). H2: Linear interpolation between n=10 and n=15, and between n=15 and n=20, provides a lower-bound extrapolation that predicts agreement at n=50. H3: The extrapolated agreement at n=50 remains below 80%, confirming the plateau is structural.
falsifier: F1: The empirical CDF mapping fails to reproduce observed agreement at training points n=15 and n=20 within 1pp (indicating data corruption or computation error). F2: Linear interpolation between n=10 and n=15 produces a slope that implies agreement crosses 80% before n=50 (indicating the plateau breaks). F3: The extrapolated proportion at n=50 exceeds 0.80, justifying Docker re-collection. F4: The step-function structure (0, 0, 0.50, 0.57) cannot be captured by any monotonic interpolation, indicating the margin distribution has non-monotonic behavior that invalidates the interpolation approach.

baselines.description: Phi(median(|M|)/std) predicted 0.8455 at n15 (residual 34.59pp) and 0.7550 at n20 (residual 18.96pp). REJECTED at C1.
Saturating sign-fraction power law fitted 0.3757 at n15 (residual 12.39pp) and 0.6395 at n20 (residual 7.41pp). R2=0.8797 <0.90. REJECTED at C1/C2.
Phi(mean/std) predicted 0.7379 at n20 (residual 17.8pp). REJECTED at C1.
Direct proportion(margin>0) = 0.4996 at n15 (residual 0.00pp) and 0.5654 at n20 (residual 0.00pp). Near-exact under template invariance.
Random noise model agreement ~50% at all n. Best validated model must outperform this null.

positive_control.description: The empirical CDF mapping reproduces observed ranking agreement at all training points (n=5, 10, 15, 20) within 1pp. This is trivially true by construction (the empirical CDF is defined at these points), but serves as a data integrity check.
positive_control.expected: Empirical CDF at n=5 within 1pp of 0.0; at n=10 within 1pp of 0.0; at n=15 within 1pp of 0.4996; at n=20 within 1pp of 0.5654.

null_control.description: Linear interpolation between adjacent training points provides a null model for extrapolation. If the empirical CDF extrapolation to n=50 is indistinguishable from linear extrapolation from n=20, the non-parametric approach adds no information beyond simple linear trend.
null_control.expected: Empirical CDF extrapolation at n=50 must differ from linear extrapolation from n=20 by >5pp to demonstrate non-trivial structure.

measurement_validity: All computations use existing data from EXP-INTEL-35476271877: snr_per_iteration_tag_entropy.json.gz (sha256 ce3dda6e021137ef0c911c19d8897c24f26342e8bd6da77242e1a026e08c1b7a) and analysis_output_snr.json (sha256 f7f6986753774125966be2654a30744de386e2ab93790b02ec84d035ff1358b2). No new data collection required. No browser/network/model calls.

The empirical CDF mapping is defined as: for each n, F(n) = proportion(margin_i > 0). This is the same statistic as the diagnostic indicator, which already matches observed agreement within 0.02pp and 0.59pp at n=15 and n=20 respectively.
The non-parametric extrapolation uses piecewise linear interpolation between training points (n=5, 10, 15, 20) and extrapolation beyond n=20 using the slope between n=15 and n=20.

Template invariance persists on truncated-first-20 subsample (verified in parent). Under template invariance, ranking agreement = proportion(margin_i > 0) exactly, so the empirical CDF mapping is the true data-generating process at training points.

The critical test is whether the step-function structure (0, 0, 0.50, 0.57) implies a threshold/phase-transition that makes linear extrapolation invalid, or whether the monotonic increase from n=10 to n=20 provides a reliable trend for extrapolation.
Primary definition: tag_entropy x DEF-FULL-MAP. Same as parent experiments.
Cart n=1 degeneracy excluded from margin computations per parent protocol.
decision_rule:
Conjunctive:

C1_EMPIRICAL_CDF_REPRODUCES_TRAINING: The empirical CDF mapping reproduces observed ranking agreement at n=15 and n=20 within 1pp. PASS if residuals <1pp at both points; FAIL otherwise. (Expected: trivially PASS by construction.)

C2_STEP_FUNCTION_STRUCTURE: The step-function structure (0, 0, 0.50, 0.57) has a monotonic increase from n=10 to n=20. PASS if proportion(20) > proportion(15) > proportion(10) > proportion(5); FAIL if non-monotonic.

C3_EXTRAPOLATION_BELOW_80: The empirical CDF extrapolation to n=50 predicts agreement < 0.80. PASS if predicted proportion at n=50 < 0.80; FAIL if >= 0.80.

VERDICT RULES:
- If NOT C1: MEASUREMENT_INVALID — data corruption or computation error.
- If C1 AND NOT C2: MEASUREMENT_INVALID — non-monotonic margin structure invalidates interpolation approach.
- If C1 AND C2 AND C3: EMPIRICAL_CDF_VALIDATED — the non-parametric mapping captures the step-function structure; extrapolation predicts plateau persists below 80%; recipe density is structurally limited; product lane should use non-recipe density.
- If C1 AND C2 AND NOT C3: EMPIRICAL_CDF_PREDICTS_CROSSING — the extrapolation predicts agreement crosses 80% at full DOM; Docker re-collection is justified; recipe density remains viable.
product_consequence_positive: If C1 AND C2 AND C3 (empirical CDF validated, predicts <80% at full DOM): The 56% plateau is structural — the step-function proportion(margin>0) saturates below 80% as n increases. Product lane should adopt non-recipe density immediately (which preserves ranking at 100%) and accept the eta2 reduction. Docker re-collection investment is NOT justified for the ranking stability question. The empirical CDF provides a validated diagnostic for any future pipeline or definition changes.
product_consequence_negative: If C1 AND C2 AND NOT C3 (empirical CDF predicts >=80% at full DOM): The plateau is predicted to break at full DOM. Docker re-collection investment is justified. Product lane should wait for full-DOM results before closing the recipe density design path.
estimated_cost: VERY LOW — offline computation on existing reconstructed data. No browser/network/model calls. The analysis requires: (1) computing empirical CDF from per-iteration margins (<5 seconds); (2) validating at training points (<1 second); (3) checking monotonicity (<1 second); (4) linear extrapolation to n=50/82 (<1 second); (5) comparing against linear null (<1 second). Total estimated <500 LLM tokens for analysis code and <10 seconds compute.
expected_information_gain: HIGH — directly tests whether the non-parametric empirical CDF approach can succeed where three parametric decompositions failed. The step-function structure (0, 0, 0.50, 0.57) suggests threshold behavior that parametric models cannot capture. Either positive (validated non-parametric extrapolation) or negative (step-function structure invalidates interpolation) outcome changes a concrete product decision about Docker re-collection investment and recipe density viability. If both parametric and non-parametric modeling fail, the Intel lane should pivot to Docker-based direct measurement as the only remaining path to an empirical answer.
